claims.claim_text: Minerals are the currency of life — the body's basic functions depend on them, and Wallach argues the medical profession ignores this truth to the point past the absurd.
claims.verbatim:
Simply said, minerals are the currency
of life. The medical profession ignores this
truth to the point past the absurd

claims.claim_text: The basic functions of life cannot be performed without minerals — either as a structural part of the function or as a catalytic cofactor (for RNA, DNA, sub-cellular and digestive enzymes, and the utilization of vitamins).
claims.verbatim:
The basic functions of life itself cannot
be performed without minerals, either as a
major part of the function or as a catalytic
cofactor

claims.claim_text: Wallach frames heat-stroke deaths (he points to the deadly July 1993 US east-coast heat wave) as a simple salt/sodium deficiency — easily remedied with water and salt, and worsened by doctor-ordered low-salt diets.
claims.verbatim:
a simple salt or sodium deficiency
(your basic heat stroke that any boy scout
could diagnose and recognize and remedy
with water and salt)

claims.claim_text: Wallach discovered the trace mineral selenium's pivotal role in the cause and prevention of cystic fibrosis while working as a research veterinary pathologist.
claims.verbatim:
a trace mineral, Selenium, in the etiology and
prevention of Cystic Fibrosis while a research veterinary pathologist

claims.claim_text: Wallach cites U.S. Senate Document 264 (1936) and the 1992 Rio Earth Summit report on soil mineral-depletion rates: the world's farm and range soils are 'anemic' — soils that should contain 60 elements have few or none.
claims.verbatim:
U.S Senate Document 264 (1936) and the 1992 Earth Summit Report (Rio) on mineral
depletion rates of the world's farm and range soils point out graphically that our Earth's soils
are anemic - the soil should contain 60 of them, there are few or none!

claims.claim_text: Wallach puts the human genetic potential for longevity at 120 to 140 years — the US average life span falls as much as 50% short of it.
claims.verbatim:
falls
far short (as much as 50% short) of our human genetic potential for longevity of 120 to 140
years.

claims.claim_text: Wallach argues the extended rat lifespans in calorie-restriction studies came not from fewer calories but from the higher concentration of minerals per calorie in the diet.
claims.verbatim:
It is not the reduced calorie level that gave the rats their extended life spans by 30, 40 and
50%, but rather it is the increased concentration of mineral per calorie in the diet

claims.claim_text: After two years of minimal-calorie intake in Biosphere II, five of the six Biospherians craved only pizza and junk food — which Wallach reads as a manifestation of pica (mineral hunger).
claims.verbatim:
five of the six Biospherians (excluding Walford) wanted only pizza
and junk food (a manifestation of pica)

claims.claim_text: Wallach frames the Earth as a finite, limited resource for the raw-material elements that are the basis of all plant, animal, and human life.
claims.verbatim:
our planet is a limited finite resource for
the raw materials that are the basis of all
plant, animal and human life as we know
it.

claims.claim_text: Wallach's theory holds that cystic fibrosis can be an acquired environmental disease produced by a deficiency of selenium, zinc, and riboflavin, and worsened by diets low in vitamin E and high in polyunsaturated fatty acids.
claims.verbatim:
an acquired environmental disease
that can be produced by a deficiency of selenium, zinc, and
riboflavin and exacerbated by diets also low in vitamin E

claims.claim_text: Germanium deficiency is typified by severely reduced immune status, arthritis, osteoporosis, low energy, and cancer.
claims.verbatim:
Deficiencies of germanium are typified
by severely reduced immune status,

claims.claim_text: Wallach gives a germanium maintenance dose of 20-30 mg/day; 50-100 mg/day is commonly used when an individual has a serious illness that requires an increased oxygen level in the body.
claims.verbatim:
50 to 100 mg per day are commonly used
when an individual has a serious illness that
requires an increased oxygen level in the
body.

claims.claim_text: Wallach lists germanium-rich foods — watercress, shiitake mushroom, pearl barley, sanzukon, sushi, waternut, boxthorn seed, and wisteria knob — at 100 to 2,000 ppm germanium.
claims.verbatim:
sanzukon, sushi, waternut, boxthorn
seed and wisteria knob contain germanium
in amounts ranging from 100 to 2,000 ppm.

claims.claim_text: Against an RDA of 3-4 mcg/day, Wallach prefers a vitamin B12/cobalt intake of 250 to 400 mcg/day, especially when preparing for pregnancy and while nursing.
claims.verbatim:
250 to 400 mcg per day, especially while
preparing for a pregnancy and nursing

claims.claim_text: Wallach holds that birth defects — physical, emotional, biochemical, and behavioral — that occur to the embryo or fetus and show up at birth are not genetic, but are in fact preventable.
claims.verbatim:
Injuries or birth defects (i.e.-physical,
emotional, biochemical and behavioral)
that occur to the embryo and fetus and
show up at birth regardless of cause are not
genetic and are in fact preventable.

claims.claim_text: Wallach attributes the higher trisomy (Down's syndrome) risk in older mothers to mineral depletion — a woman depleted of minerals by her mid-30s carries higher-risk embryos.
claims.verbatim:
(the poor woman would be depleted
of minerals by the time she was over 35 so
the last two or three embryos were at higher
tisk for trisomy)

claims.claim_text: Every species has a genetic-potential ceiling for longevity — Wallach lists mice ~700 days, dogs 23 years, horses 32, elephants 45, chimpanzees 52, and humans 145 years.
claims.verbatim:
All species have a “genetic potential” or
upper limit for longevity - mice 700 days,
dogs 23 years, horses 32 years, elephant
45 years, chimpanzee 52 years and man
145 years

claims.claim_text: Reaching the 145-year longevity potential requires consuming each of the 90 essential nutrients in optimal amounts every day.
claims.verbatim:
Do those positive things necessary
to make it to 145 including consuming each
of the 90 essential nutrients in optimal
amounts each day.
